name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 17, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the
City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:01 p.m.,
on October 17, 2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 12, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title “Council Member.”

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Ury
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  W. Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the

City Council Minutes  1  October 17, 2011
   Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employee (Assistant City
  Manager.) The City’s Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council commenced discussions for item CS1
and they will resume the closed session deliberations at the conclusion of the meeting. Mr.
Curley requested that the City Council remove item 12 from the open session agenda and the
matter will be considered, as appropriate, at a later date.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Musical Presentation

  Mission Viejo High School students Kenny Davis and Jean-Luc Rollando sang a duet for
  the City Council and audience.

P2.  Recognize Mission Viejo’s Community Recycling Program Award Winners

  Michelle Clark of Waste Management presented the award to Sue DeCant, Engage Life
  Director for Atria Del Sol senior living community.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Tammy Descoteaux, Orange County Sheriff’s Department: reminded residents of the 23rd
annual Walk Against Drugs on October 22, 2011, beginning at 8:00 a.m. at Mission Viejo High
School. The rally begins with keynote speaker Mark Munoz, Ultimate Fighting Middleweight
Championship contender. Participants will then walk up La Paz Road to the Disaster
Preparedness Expo and Fair on the Village Green at the Murray Community Center.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: thanked the Mayor for doing a wonderful job at the Mission Viejo Chamber
of Commerce grand opening. He also expressed concern with item 12 on the agenda and read
from a blog post written by resident Geoff Willis who is opposed to the contract with Assistant
City Manager Rattay.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed opposition to the OCFA Budget and Finance Committee’s

City Council Minutes  2  October 17, 2011
 recommendation to the OCFA Executive Committee that they renew agreements with UBS
Financial Services and Wells Fargo. He asked Council Member Kelley, as a member of the
OCFA Executive Committee, to instruct the OCFA Treasurer to seek competitive bids.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: referred to a recent newspaper article regarding the release of
approximately 25 prisoners a month from the Orange County jail and she reminded residents that
there is a neighborhood watch program in Mission Viejo. Mrs. Bucknum also shared the news
that Gene Cox, the “voice of the Nadadores,” passed away very suddenly on Thursday and she
asked that the meeting be adjourned in his memory.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 11 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  (1) Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of October 3, 2011, as
  presented; and (2) approved the Minutes for the special City Council Meeting of October
  7, 2011, as presented.

3.  Check Register dated September 23, 2011 in the amount of $3,090,612.17

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated September 30, 2011 in the amount of $1,735,822.46

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  October 17, 2011
 5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2011

  Received and filed.

6.  Community Development Agency (CDA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August
  2011

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2011

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August
  2011

  Received and filed.

9.  Amend Library Holiday Hours for 2012 Calendar Year

  Close the Library from Monday, December 24 - Friday, December 28, 2012. Remain
  open on MLK day, January 16, Presidents’ Day, January 20 and Veterans’ Day, Sunday,
  November 11, 2012. The total number of hours the library is open to the public
  throughout the year will remain the same.

10.  Shade Structure Seating Area at the Mission Viejo Animal Service Center

  (1) Adopted Resolution 11-67 Amending the Fiscal year 2011-2012 Budget for the Cost
  Related to the Mission Viejo Animal Services Center Shade Structure and Seating Area;
  (2) authorized staff to proceed with the construction of the shade structure and seating
  area at the Mission Viejo Animal Shelter; and (3) approved the First Amendment to the
  contract with S. Parker Engineering in an amount not to exceed $30,000.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

12.  Employment Contract for Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, W.
  Keith Rattay

  This item was not considered.

NEW BUSINESS

City Council Minutes  4  October 17, 2011
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

11.  Operating Agreement for a Farmers Market at the Mission Viejo Civic Center

  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, presented the staff
  report.

  Council Member Reardon asked questions and requested that staff provide the City
  Council with a list of costs associated with the farmers market (staff time, marketing,
  etc.)

  The following presented a written comment in favor of the Farmer’s Market: Joni Marie
  O’Neill, owner of Mission Viejo Florist.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve
  the Operating Agreement with Verge Hagopian (Market Operator) to set up and operate a
  Farmers Market at the Civic Center on a weekly basis and authorize the Mayor to sign the
  Agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

13.  Community Services Commission Vacancy

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to receive
  the letter of resignation from Commissioner Edwin Althof and direct the City Clerk to
  place an item on the November 7, 2011, City Council agenda for appointment of a new
  Community Services Commissioner.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

14.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

City Council Minutes  5  October 17, 2011
   Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that privatization of OCFA services at John Wayne
  airport could mean potential savings of 50% and he alluded to a behind the scenes deal
  between the Union president and the OCFA fire captains.

15.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury presented the report and shared a PowerPoint presentation on the
  initial segment of the 241 completion project from Oso Parkway to the vicinity of Ortega
  Highway.

16.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness announced that he had nothing to report on the San Joaquin Hills TCA.

17.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Attorney’s Report

18.  Verbal Update on Newly Adopted AB 1236: Elimination of Everify Authority

  City Attorney Curley presented the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

19.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley reminded residents of the Walk Against Drugs on Saturday, October 22,
beginning at 8:00 a.m. She apologized in advance for having to miss the event because she will
be out of town. Council Member Kelley also reminded residents that Capistrano Valley High
School is hosting a “Taste of Capo” fundraiser on Thursday, October 20. There are over 20 local
restaurants participating in the event as well as various activities and a silent auction. Tickets are

City Council Minutes  6  October 17, 2011
 $15 in advance and $20 at the door. She also announced that the City’s Hometown Halloween
will be held on October 29, 2011, from 4:00 to 8:00 p.m. at the Norman P. Murray Community
Center. Council Member Kelley concluded her comments by expressing her sadness at the
passing of resident Gene Cox and she agreed that the meeting should be adjourned in his
memory.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon announced that she and Mayor Leckness attended “Let’s Jump” at
Castille Elementary School and she enjoyed watching more than 500 students in their attempt to
break a world record. She also outlined her attendance at two recent meetings regarding the San
Onofre nuclear power plant. She noted that her awareness has been heightened and she thinks
that Southern California Edison has some significant issues with the power plant including the
age of the facility and evacuation plans. Council Member Reardon announced that she will bring
some information to the Council and to staff so that the City can inform residents of the issues.
She also mentioned the address for the Union of Concerned Scientists web site at www.ucs.org
and she recognized that there are two sides to the issues and the web site publicizes just one side.
Council Member Reardon announced that Saddleback College has posted its 2 nd annual resume
survey. It has some great information and recommendations and she encouraged high school
students, college students, and those that are out of a job to read the survey on the college’s web
site or on the Mission Viejo Dispatch.

Council Member Schlicht

20.  An Ordinance to Establish Our City Parks and Trails as CHILD SAFETY ZONES
  by Banning Registered Sexual Predators From Entering Our Parks and Trails
  Without Written Permission From the Orange County Sheriff

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  Kelly Higgins, M.V.: expressed support for the proposed ordinance.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to direct
  the City Attorney to model a “Child Safety Zone” City Ordinance using Orange County
  Ordinance No. 03-18-1 to 6 as the prototype.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  7  October 17, 2011
 Council Member Schlicht reminded residents that the AlertOC system will be tested on October
20, 2011. She encouraged residents to register with this mass notification system so they will be
informed during an emergency. She also noted that residents can find information on adequately
preparing their home for an emergency by calling (714) 828-7085. Council Member Schlicht
announced that she is a charter member of the new Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce. She
enjoyed the grand opening event and she expects that it will be a very successful chamber
chapter. Lastly, Council Member Schlicht asked Mayor Leckness to close the meeting in
memory of the victims of the Seal Beach massacre.

Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness announced that he has just completed two new City Talk programs for Mission
Viejo Television (MVTV) which will air weeknights at 6:00 p.m. on channel 30. The shows
focus on his visit to the highest point in Mission Viejo, a Mission Viejo sewer line, the local
sewer treatment plant, and a walk along the Oso Creek Trail. He also touched on his attendance
at the Castille Elementary School “Let’s Jump” program and the Chamber of Commerce grand
opening event. In addition, Mayor Leckness stated that he had the honor of presenting an award
to Father Bruce at St. Killian Catholic Church last evening. He also reminded residents to attend
the Walk Against Drugs on Saturday, October 22 and his all night Camp Out with the Mayor the
same afternoon, beginning at 4:00 p.m. along the Oso Creek Trail. The YMCA is co-sponsoring
the program and Mayor Leckness stated that it is destined to become one of the greatest events in
Mission Viejo.

CLOSED SESSION (Continued)

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employee (Assistant City
  Manager.) The City’s Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 7:03 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 8:49 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

City Council Minutes  8  October 17, 2011
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:50 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting in memory of Gene Cox, Loren Anderson, and the
victims of the Seal Beach massacre, to Monday, November 7, 2011, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 7, 2011

City Council Minutes  9  October 17, 2011
